reasons.next-verse-12-23: LXX2012 carries English of the next Greek verse in these two (Genesis 13:11 'And Abram lived in the land of Chanaan' is Swete's 13:12; Genesis 22:15 runs into 22:16; Genesis 23:5's 'Not so, Sir,' is Swete's 23:6 'Μὴ κύριε'): the Greek words are in the other verse (mw-u2w5klk.349.3).
reasons.added-15-23: Brenton's English adds it to make a Greek phrase English, and the Greek verse has no word for it ('is my heir' and 'am grieved' of 15:2 and 15:3, 'to the porch' of 19:6, 'a small one' of 19:20, 'to go' of 19:27, 'saying' of 19:38, 'the land is worth' and 'nay, do' of 23:15); each was read against its verse and no Greek word of a neighbouring chunk renders it (mw-u2w5klk.349.83).
reasons.paired-or-added-12-23: Either the Greek word that renders it is a pair the aligner made to another English word that no fix row has yet moved ('God' for αἰώνιον in 17:19, paired to the word before it: the Greek has no 'God' there), or Brenton's English adds it to turn a Greek phrase into English ('forth', 'aside', 'early', 'fine', 'aloud', 'only', 'still', 'drink', 'journey') (mw-u2w5klk.349.3).
reasons.added-14: Brenton adds 'Lord' of 14:22 to make English of a Greek phrase (τὸν θεὸν τὸν ὕψιστον has no κύριον) (mw-u2w5klk.349.23).
reasons.other-verse-24-29: Brenton's English of these verses carries a clause whose Greek word is in the verse before or after (Genesis 24:18 'till', 24:27 'and said', 25:20 'Abraam begot Isaac', 27:44 'until your brother's anger') or that the Greek verse does not have (27:38 'being troubled, Esau cried aloud and wept', 29:20 'and they were before him as a few days, by reason of his loving her') (mw-u2w5klk.349.4).
reasons.paired-or-added-24-29: The Greek word that renders it is a pair the aligner made to another English word ('draw' for ὑδρεύσατο) or English Brenton adds to make a Greek phrase English ('instead', 'just', 'hither', 'forth', 'away') (mw-u2w5klk.349.4).
reasons.other-verse-30-36: LXX2012 carries English here whose Greek is in the verse before or after (Genesis 31:50 to 31:53's 'God is witness', 'swore by the Fear of his father Isaac', 30:9's 'went in', which Swete has in 30:10), or English that the Greek verse does not have (Genesis 31:51 is a whole verse with no Greek, 33:5's 'Esau', 35:29's 'Isaac', 36:18's 'daughter of Ana, wife of Esau') (mw-u2w5klk.349.5).
reasons.paired-or-added-30-36: Either the Greek word that renders it is a pair the aligner made to another English word ('lord' for Κύριος, 'hand' for χειρός, 'stead' for ἀντί) or Brenton adds it to make English of a Greek phrase ('forth', 'away', 'back', 'matter', 'hard', 'very', 'looked') (mw-u2w5klk.349.5).
reasons.next-verse-37-39: LXX2012's 37:32 holds the Greek 37:32 and 37:33 (docs/data.md), so 'And he recognized it, and said, It is my son's coat, an evil wild beast has devoured him; a wild beast has carried off Joseph.' renders the words of the Greek verse 37:33, which has no English chunk of its own to point at (mw-u2w5klk.349.47).
reasons.added-37-39: Brenton adds them to make English of a Greek phrase: 37:2 'of his father' (Swete has only 'with his brethren'), 37:8 'shall you indeed be lord' and 'still more' (ἔτι is 'still'), 37:24 'was empty' (Swete: 'had no water'), 38:9 'to his brother's wife' (Swete: 'to his brother'), 38:17 'Well,' and 39:12 'in her hands,' (Swete: 'having left his clothes, he fled') (mw-u2w5klk.349.47).
reasons.conflated-40-42: LXX2012's 41:27 gives 'the seven thin and blasted ears are seven years; there shall be seven years of famine' for a Greek 'the seven ears ... shall be seven years of famine', so the clause 'are seven years;' has no Greek word (mw-u2w5klk.349.48).
reasons.added-40-42: Brenton adds them to make English of a Greek phrase: 41:12 'our dreams' ('we related to him', διηγησάμεθα αὐτῷ), 41:16 'be given' (ἀποκριθήσεται, 'an answer shall be given'), 41:52 'said he', and 42:4 'Jacob' (Swete: 'he sent not', ἀπέστειλεν; the name is Brenton's) (mw-u2w5klk.349.48).
reasons.added-43-45: Brenton adds them to make English of a Greek phrase: 43:3 'the lord of the country,' (Swete has only 'ὁ ἄνθρωπος'), 43:6 'inasmuch as' (εἰ) and 43:32 'on bread for' (Swete's ἄρτους is the 'bread' of 'eat bread', later in the verse) (mw-u2w5klk.349.49).
reasons.previous-verse-44: LXX2012's 44:5 'Why have you stolen my silver cup?' renders the end of the Greek verse 44:4 (ἵνα τί ἐκλέψατέ μου τὸ κόνδυ τὸ ἀργυροῦν), which has no English chunk of its own to point at (the like of Genesis 37:32) (mw-u2w5klk.349.49).
reasons.hebrew-only-45: 45:4 'Joseph said to his brethren, Draw near to me; and they drew near; and he said,' is Brenton's from the Hebrew: Swete's Greek has only 'And he said, I am Joseph your brother' (mw-u2w5klk.349.49).
reasons.other-verse-46-48: LXX2012 carries English here whose Greek is in another verse: Genesis 46:13's 'of Phares were Esron, ... Jemuel. And the sons of' renders the end of the Greek verse 46:12 (ἐγένοντο δὲ υἱοὶ Φάρες Ἁσρὼμ καὶ Ἰεμουήλ), and 47:4 holds, after its own Greek ('we will dwell in the land of Gesem'), the English of the Greek verse 47:5 (Κατοικείτωσαν ἐν γῇ Γέσεμ ... ἤκουσεν Φαραώ): a chunk can point only at a Greek word of its own verse, so the 47:5 Greek words are left with no English and these words with no Greek (mw-u2w5klk.349.50).
reasons.added-46-48: Brenton adds them to make English of a Greek phrase, or English the Greek does not have: 46:6 and 48:5 'the land of' Egypt (Swete: εἰς Αἴγυπτον, ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ), 46:7 'his daughters;' (Swete's second 'of his sons' is υἱῶν), 46:8 'with their father' (Swete: 'Jacob and his sons'), 46:27 'with Joseph' (Swete: 'who came into Egypt'), 47:18 'are indeed destitute.' (Swete ends 'and our land') and 48:11 'of seeing' (Swete: 'of your face') (mw-u2w5klk.349.50).
reasons.other-verse-49-50: LXX2012's 49:2 opens with the English of the Greek verse 49:1 ('Assemble yourselves, that I may tell you what shall happen to you in the last days.' renders Συνάχθητε, ἵνα ἀναγγείλω ὑμῖν τί ἀπαντήσει ὑμῖν ἐπ᾽ ἐσχάτων τῶν ἡμέρων), so those words of 49:1 have no English chunk to point at and these words have no Greek of their own verse: the like of Genesis 37:32 (mw-u2w5klk.349.51).
reasons.added-49-50: Brenton adds them to make English of a Greek phrase, or English the Greek does not have: 50:6 'to Joseph,' (Swete: Εἶπεν Φαραώ Ἀνάβηθι), 50:15 'Let us take heed,' (Swete: Μή ποτε begins the speech), 50:20 'the matter' (Swete: ὅπως ἂν γενηθῇ ὡς σήμερον) and 50:26 'aged' (Swete: ἐτῶν ἑκατὸν δέκα, whose 'years' is the aligner's) (mw-u2w5klk.349.51).
